name: Mumbai and Goa: Mumbai, Anjuna and Assagao, Palolem

cities.base: Colaba or Kala Ghoda in Fort: the Gateway, CSMVS, Leopold, Mondegar and Kala Ghoda Cafe are all within 1.5 km on foot, and the Elephanta boats leave from the Gateway.
cities.name: Mumbai

cities.base: Assagao for quiet and the better kitchens (Vinayak, Jamun), or the Anjuna strip for beach shacks; Old Goa is about 20 km off either way, so hire a car or scooter.
cities.name: North Goa: Anjuna and Assagao

cities.base: The Palolem to Patnem road, with every restaurant here inside 2 km. The sights run 14 to 74 km away, so a car is the plan; Madgaon is the train terminus from Mumbai.
cities.name: South Goa: Palolem

places.name: The Bombay Canteen
places.note: Modern Indian, Google 4.5 from 10,943 reviews: order the duck momos, tandoori lamb chops and seabass sev puri, about Rs 1,700 for two. Lunch to 15:30, dinner from 19:00, Sunday is lunch 11:00 to 15:00, and it is 9 km north of Colaba, so a taxi.

places.name: Kala Ghoda Cafe
places.note: Google 4.4 from 5,699 reviews; masala cappuccino, waffles, sandwiches and carrot cake, about Rs 1,000 for two. Open 08:00 to midnight and 200 m from CSMVS, so it is the breakfast before the museum.

places.name: Cafe Mondegar
places.note: The old Colaba Causeway cafe with the jukebox, Google 4.4 from 6,048 reviews. Order butter mushrooms, fish and chips or the roast pork sausages, Rs 1,200 to 1,300 for two; EazyDiner lists a 07:30 start.

places.name: Leopold Cafe & Bar
places.note: The Causeway cafe-bar hit in the 26/11 attacks, bullet holes still in the walls; Google 4.2 from 32,854 reviews. Mutton biryani and cocktails. Magicpin's 2026 figure is Rs 2,500 for two, EazyDiner says Rs 1,200, so budget the higher.

places.name: Gateway of India
places.note: George Wittet's basalt arch, begun 1913 and opened 1924 for George V's 1911 landing; the last British troops left through it in February 1948. Free, open round the clock; go early, and buy Elephanta boat tickets at the official counters, not from touts.

places.name: Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Vastu Sangrahalaya (CSMVS)
places.note: Wittet's 1915 building, a museum since 1922, with about 50,000 objects: Indus Valley finds, Gupta terracottas, Elephanta sculptures, Akbar-era armour, miniatures. Foreigner ticket about 10 dollars on Klook; give it two hours from opening. Google 4.6.

places.name: Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus (CSMT)
places.note: F. W. Stevens' Victorian Gothic terminus of 1878 to 1887, from Axel Haig's design, a UNESCO site that still runs trains. Free to look at: find the octagonal dome, the Star Chamber and the lion and tiger at the gate, and skip the commuter peaks.

places.name: Dr Bhau Daji Lad Museum
places.note: Mumbai's oldest museum, opened 1855 as the Victoria and Albert, in a restored Palladian hall of decorative arts with a 19th-century city gallery. Closed Wednesdays; Rs 20 for Indians, foreigner rate not found, so check the price. Beside the zoo.

places.name: Mani Bhavan Gandhi Sangrahalaya
places.note: Gandhi's Mumbai base from 1917 to 1934: his room with the floor bed and spinning wheels, and the terrace where he was arrested on 4 January 1932. Rs 20, Google 4.6, and an hour is enough.

places.name: National Museum of Indian Cinema
places.note: Two buildings, opened 2019, on how Indian film began: archive footage and the machines that shot it; Google 4.6. Closed Mondays. A booking site lists 6.32 dollars, Time Out gave Rs 165 for Indians.

places.name: Elephanta Caves
places.note: UNESCO since 1987: 5th to 7th century rock-cut Shaiva caves, the Sadashiva Trimurti in Cave 1, 120 steps up. Closed Mondays. Ferry from the Gateway an hour each way, Rs 200 to 250 return, entry Rs 550 to 600; take the 09:00 boat, last back 17:30.

places.name: Haji Ali Dargah
places.note: A tomb-mosque on an islet at the end of a 1 km causeway that floods at high tide, so read the tide table first. Free and open to all faiths; Thursdays and Fridays are the busiest. Hours vary, check.

places.name: Crawford Market (Mahatma Jyotiba Phule Market)
places.note: The covered market completed in 1869, with entrance friezes carved by John Lockwood Kipling, a kilometre north of CSMT. Hours vary, check; go in the morning.

places.name: Kanheri Caves
places.note: 109 Buddhist caves cut between the 1st and 10th centuries CE inside Sanjay Gandhi National Park, about 30 km north of Colaba; Google 4.5. Gate hours and ticket not found, so check the price; a half day with the drive.

places.name: Baba Au Rhum
places.note: French-style cafe, Google 4.4 from 14,830 reviews: shakshuka and croissants in the morning, thin-crust pizza and craft beer later. Rs 800 to 1,200 for two. It shuts 17:00 to 18:00, and Tuesday has no evening sitting.

places.name: Jamun Goa
places.note: Google 4.5 from 2,388 reviews: ghee roast chicken with Malabar parotta, Goan fish curry, jackfruit biryani. Rs 1,800 for two and reviewers call it dear. Lunch to 15:30, dinner from 19:00.

places.name: Vinayak Family Restaurant
places.note: The Goan family place, Google 4.3 from 9,700 reviews: crab masala, kingfish rawa fry, tisryo clams, the fish thali, bebinca. Most dishes under Rs 500. Closed Thursdays, and shut from 16:30 (17:00 weekends) to 19:00.

places.name: Babka Goa
places.note: Bakery-cafe for the signature babka, quiche, cakes and all-day breakfast; Google 4.3 from 2,720 reviews, about Rs 850 for two. Closed Mondays. One listing says it closes at 20:00, so come before 18:30 to be safe.

places.name: Elephant and Co.
places.note: Dinner and drinks by Anjuna beach, Google 4.7 from 1,747 reviews: Ross omelette with poi, Moroccan chicken, dumplings, the gin and curry-leaf cocktail. Rs 2,000 for two; to 01:00 on Wednesday, Friday and Saturday.

places.name: Cafe Lilliput
places.note: The old Anjuna beach shack, Google 3.9 from 9,843 reviews, with live music some nights and techno on others; about Rs 900 for two. Hours vary, check.

places.name: Basilica of Bom Jesus
places.note: Built 1594 to 1605 to hold the body of St Francis Xavier, UNESCO since 1986; the relics come down for the decennial exposition. Free. About 20 km from Anjuna, so go early by car; Sunday Mass is at 07:00, 08:00 and 09:15.

places.name: Se Cathedral
places.note: The Cathedral of St Catherine, about 91 m long, built to mark the 1510 victory, 300 m from Bom Jesus. Free, with a donation box. Hours not found, so pair it with Bom Jesus in the morning.

places.name: Archaeological Museum of Goa
places.note: Beside the church of St Francis of Assisi: Hindu temple fragments, sati stones, the viceroys' portraits and a bronze Albuquerque. Closed Fridays; a reviewer paid Rs 10. Google 4.3.
places.neighborhood: Old Goa, by St Francis of Assisi

places.name: Museum of Christian Art
places.note: Christian art in the Convent of Santa Monica, 500 m west of Bom Jesus; Google 4.4. About Rs 100 an adult, open daily to 16:30.
places.neighborhood: Convent of Santa Monica, Old Goa

places.name: Reis Magos Fort
places.note: A fort of 1551, a prison until 1993, restored from 2008 as a cultural centre; Google 4.4 from 11,376 reviews. Free admission. Closed Mondays.

places.name: Fort Aguada
places.note: The 1612 fort over Sinquerim, with an 1864 lighthouse and a water tank of 2,376,000 gallons. Hours and ticket not found, so check the price; late afternoon for the view.

places.name: Museum of Goa (MOG)
places.note: Contemporary art with no permanent collection, so look up the current show before you drive out; Google 4.1. Rs 300 an adult, last entry 17:00, closed Mondays.

places.name: Houses of Goa Museum
places.note: Gerard da Cunha's ship-shaped museum of Goan houses, with the Mario Gallery; Google 4.2 from 4,110 reviews. About 1.60 dollars on the official listing. Closed Mondays.

places.name: Dropadi Bar And Restaurant
places.note: Beachfront bar and restaurant, Google 4.0, Tripadvisor 4.2 from 1,167 reviews: rava fish, crab curry, chilli garlic prawns, pomfret recheado. Rs 1,400 for two, or Rs 600 to 900 a head by one review; it is also the evening drink.

places.name: Nireas - Healthy Haven
places.note: Vegan, Indian and Italian, Google 4.7 and Tripadvisor 4.8, shown open in October 2026: bagel omelette, smoothie bowls, wraps, carrot cake. About Rs 1,000 for two.

places.name: Sumaya Authentic Goan Cuisine
places.note: Goan cooking, Google 4.2: the kingfish or pomfret thali, fish curry, rawa fry prawns, aubergine curry, Rs 1,300 for two. Another listing gives 11:00 to 22:00, so do not leave dinner late.

places.name: The Mill Cafe
places.note: Breakfast and lunch in a restored rice mill, Google 4.3 from 1,713 reviews: Zanzibar burger, basil cashew fettuccine, pancakes, about Rs 1,600 for two. No dinner, whatever one blog says.

places.name: Karma Cafe - Bakery
places.note: Vegetarian and vegan bakery near the Colomb mosque: juices, lassis, vegan croissants, smoothie bowls, breakfasts from Rs 250; Google 4.4. Seasonal, October to April, so shut through the monsoon.

places.name: Sushi Cafe
places.note: Sushi, wood-fired pizza and veg ramen, Google 4.3 and Tripadvisor 4.3; eight pieces of sushi run Rs 400 to 500. Opens at 16:00 and is closed Tuesdays.

places.name: Palolem Beach
places.note: A crescent of about 1.6 km with rocky ends, and the reason to sleep down here. Free; stay for the sunset off Monkey Island.

places.name: Cabo de Rama Fort
places.note: Taken by the Portuguese from the Raja of Soonda in the 1760s and a prison until 1955, with the Capela de Santo Antonio inside and cliffs below. Hours and ticket not found, check the price; 14 km from Palolem, go late afternoon.

places.name: Menezes Braganza House
places.note: A Chandor family house on land granted in 1576, 24 windows across the facade, with chandeliers, a library and a chapel relic; about Rs 450 a head, open daily, Google 4.3. 28 km from Palolem, so pair it with Goa Chitra.

places.name: Holy Spirit Church, Margao
places.note: Margao's church, built 1564 to 1565, with a German organ. Free; hours not found, so look in on the way to Chandor or Benaulim.

places.name: Palacio do Deao
places.note: The old house in Quepem, Google 4.4 from 760 reviews, 25 km from Palolem. Closed Wednesdays. Admission not found, so check the price; the Rs 1,700 figure you will see is a meal package, not a ticket.

places.name: Goa Chitra Museum
places.note: About 4,000 farm and household objects from village Goa, seen on a guided tour; Rs 300 an adult, open daily, Google 4.3 from 3,398 reviews. 29 km from Palolem.

places.name: Big Foot Goa (Ancestral Goa)
places.note: An open-air model of old rural Goa, Google 4.1 from 9,073 reviews; one reviewer paid Rs 150. 37 km from Palolem. The page gives both 17:30 and 18:00 as closing, so arrive by 16:00.

places.name: Indian Naval Aviation Museum
places.note: Google 4.6 from 7,576 reviews. Closed Mondays; Rs 150 by one count, but sources disagree, so check the price. It is 74 km from Palolem, so it belongs on the drive north, not a day of its own.

places.name: Cotigao Wildlife Sanctuary
places.note: 85.65 sq km of forest set up as a sanctuary in 1968, trails from 500 m to 5 km and a 25 m treetop watchtower; go at dawn. About Rs 100 an adult by one review, foreigner rate not found, check the price. 20 km from Palolem.

places.name: Britannia & Co
places.note: Parsi lunch room: order the berry pulao and the caramel custard, about Rs 500 for two on EazyDiner (undated, so expect more). It is cash only, closed Sunday, serves weekday lunch to 16:00, and the pulao can run out, so arrive before 13:00.

places.name: The Table
places.note: Colaba's splurge dinner, Google 4.6 from 3,163 reviews: order the oysters, warm crab and lasagne, about Rs 4,000 for two on EazyDiner. Lunch runs 12:00 to 14:30 and dinner 19:00 to 23:00 per EazyDiner (other listings run later), and it fills up, so book.

places.name: Bomras
places.note: Burmese cooking in a garden, Google 4.6 from 3,977 reviews: order the tea leaf salad and the khowsuey, about Rs 2,300 for two on District. Closed Wednesday, and the garden tables go first, so arrive by 19:30.

places.name: Chapora Fort
places.note: Portuguese border fort of 1617 on an older Muslim site; the Marathas took it in 1684 and 1739, and the Portuguese left it in 1892. The ruins hold tunnel entrances and old tombstones, with sea and river views from the top. No ticket price found, check the price; about 100 to 150 steps, no toilets, go

destination.name: Mumbai and Goa: Mumbai, Anjuna and Assagao, Palolem
destination.pitch: Two nights in Mumbai for the Victorian Gothic, the museums and Elephanta, then five in Goa: Assagao kitchens and the Old Goa churches up north, the Palolem crescent and the Chandor houses down south. Hire a car in Goa.
destination.caveat: Mumbai to Madgaon is 581 km, 7h45 on the Vande Bharat and up to 10h in the monsoon. In Goa the churches, forts and houses sit 15 to 75 km from the beach beds, so you need a car or scooter. Mondays shut Elephanta, Reis Magos and four museums. Put together for you just now from a live search, so check anything you're pinning the trip on.

because.city: Colaba and Kala Ghoda on foot: Leopold's 26/11 bullet holes, Mondegar's jukebox, Kala Ghoda Cafe at 08:00, then a taxi 9 km up to Kamala Mills for dinner at the Bombay Canteen.
because.food: Duck momos at the Bombay Canteen, crab masala and kingfish rawa fry at Vinayak in Assagao, ghee roast chicken at Jamun, and a kingfish thali at Sumaya in Palolem for Rs 1,300 for two.
because.culture: CSMT and the Gateway of India, 50,000 objects at CSMVS, the Trimurti on Elephanta, Gandhi's room at Mani Bhavan, then St Francis Xavier in Bom Jesus and the 1576 Braganza house in Chandor.
because.relaxation: Palolem is a 1.6 km crescent with rocky ends and the sunset off Monkey Island, with breakfast at Nireas or Karma and the Cotigao treetop tower for a dawn outing.
because.exploration: Old Goa's churches and the Archaeological Museum in a morning, Reis Magos and Aguada forts, Cabo de Rama on its cliffs, and Kanheri's 109 Buddhist caves 30 km north of Colaba.
